things.name: Bowling Green House
things.who: remodelled by Batty Langley for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, on an earlier building (possibly an early-eighteenth-century deer house); the main walls are dated 1720–1721 by English Heritage

things.name: the lead urns at Bowling Green House
things.who: probably by John Van Nost the Younger, copies of carved urns by Edward Pearce and Cibber

things.name: the amphitheatre by the bowling green
things.who: added north of the bowling green during the Duke of Kent's works of 1729

things.name: the serpentine canal
things.who: made during the Duke of Kent's works of 1729; Capability Brown joined it to Old Park Water about 1760

things.name: the West Half House
things.who: built for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, as a garden shelter; no architect is recorded

things.name: the East Half House
things.who: built for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, as a pair with the West Half House; the architect is unknown

things.name: the statue of the lady reading
things.who: probably made by John Cheere; Historic England says it shows Jemima, Marchioness Grey, but Bedfordshire Archives says the Duke of Kent's first wife, Jemima, who died in 1728

things.name: the Duke's Great Garden
things.who: laid out for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, with the architects Nicholas Hawksmoor and Thomas Archer, and Batty Langley and William Kent; English Heritage dates it from 1706 into the 1720s

things.name: John Rocque's plans of the garden
things.who: drawn by John Rocque, recording the Duke of Kent's gardens and garden buildings

things.name: the War of the Spanish Succession
things.who: fought by Britain, the Dutch Republic and the Habsburg Emperor against France and Spain over the Spanish throne; the Habsburg claimant was Archduke Charles

people.name: Henry Grey, Duke of Kent
people.who: the owner who made the Great Garden; created Duke of Kent in 1710; grandfather of Jemima, Marchioness Grey
events: became Marquess of Kent and began the Great Garden
was made Duke of Kent, giving up the post of Lord Chamberlain
was made a Knight of the Garter
had the East and West Half Houses built
had Batty Langley remodel Bowling Green House (about 1735)
died; the Marquess Grey title and Wrest passed to his granddaughter Jemima

people.name: Batty Langley
people.who: the garden designer and pattern-book writer who remodelled Bowling Green House
events: remodelled Bowling Green House at Wrest (about 1735)
published Ancient Architecture, Restored, and Improved

people.name: John Cheere
people.who: the London maker of garden statues, credited with several lead ones at Wrest
events: probably made the lead statue of a woman reading at Wrest (about 1748)

people.name: Jemima, Marchioness Grey
people.who: the granddaughter and heir of Henry Grey, Duke of Kent; wife of Philip Yorke, who became 2nd Earl of Hardwicke in 1764
events: inherited Wrest when her grandfather died on 5 June
